name: Arravex
description: Arravex is a noradrenergic and dopaminergic confidence modulator that suppresses the neural correlates of self-doubt and social threat appraisal while elevating assertiveness, vocal projection, and executive social behavior. Unlike crude stimulants, it targets specifically the prefrontal circuits governing self-assessment, producing confident behavior that reads as genuine rather than manic or aggressive. It was originally developed for Helix's executive performance program and has since become the standard chemical preparation for high-stakes corporate presentations, negotiations, and legal proceedings.
effects: marked increase in self-assessed and observed confidence
improved vocal quality and public speaking performance
side_effects: overconfidence errors — impaired recognition of genuine personal limitations
interpersonal friction if used in settings where assertiveness is unwelcome
comedown characterized by acute self-doubt and vulnerability
rare: grandiosity cascade in users with latent narcissistic profiles
tolerance develops with frequent use, requiring dose escalation
cultural_context: Arravex has transformed GLMZ's professional culture. Job interviews, promotion assessments, and contract negotiations are now understood to be Arravex events — everyone knows everyone is on it, and interviewers are on it too. There's a dark irony in performance reviews conducted entirely by chemically confident people assessing chemically confident candidates. On the Shelf, a rougher street version called 'swagger' produces more aggressive confidence with less social finesse — useful in confrontations and gang hierarchy disputes. The drug has been quietly introduced into corporate team offsite events through beverage dosing, a practice that is technically illegal and widely practiced.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 man discovers he's been secretly dosed with Arravex by his corporate employer for months — the confidence he's built his new life around isn't his. He needs to know who authorized it and whether he can ever trust himself again.

A Tier 4 corporate lawyer won a landmark case that put a Shelf gang leader away for life. She's just realized she was on a double dose of Arravex during every court appearance and is no longer certain the performance was real — or that the verdict was just.

Helix is developing a next-generation version of Arravex that also suppresses the user's ability to detect deception — making them not just confident but permanently persuadable. Someone wants the prototype formula.
